# Game Systems Design

## Player Stats (4 stats, each 1-10)
- **Vibe** — Natural language fluency with AI
- **Architecture** — System design & agent thinking
- **Protocol** — Integration & MCP knowledge
- **Command** — Leadership of multi-agent systems

## Ranks (based on combined stat total)
- Cadet (4-10) — Act 1
- Navigator (11-20) — Act 2
- Commander (21-30) — Act 3
- Admiral (31-40) — Academy unlocked

## Character Creation
- Choose callsign (name)
- Choose ship (3 cosmetic options)
- Intro text crawl cinematic

## Mission Structure
Briefing → Learning phase → Challenge → Debrief
Each planet has 3-5 missions.

## Mission/Challenge Types
1. **Prompt Duel** — Write best natural language prompt, scored
2. **Architect** — Drag-and-drop system diagram building
3. **Connect** — Draw connections in visual puzzle (MCP wiring)
4. **Debug** — Find problems in code/architecture
5. **Command** — Assign right agents to right tasks
6. **Dialogue** — NPC quiz-conversations

## Crew Members (map to agent loop)
- ARIA — Ship AI/narrator (start of game)
- Scout — Perception specialist (Agent Academy)
- Archie — Planning/reasoning (Agent Academy M3)
- Exec — Action/execution (Framework Nebula)
- Mirror — Reflection/testing (Security Fortress)

## Inventory
Items = real tools with in-game names:
- Ship Voice Module = Claude Code/Cursor
- Context Adapter = MCP
- Agent Blueprint = Agent architecture pattern
- Fleet Comm Array = Multi-agent orchestration
- Security Shield = HITL framework
- Local Core = Ollama/Local LLMs
- Skill Chips = Claude Code skills/plugins

## Save System
- localStorage auto-save after every mission
- No password gating — progression earned through completion
- "New Game" reset option

### Animate Component Exit with `AnimatePresence` (React)

Source: https://motion.dev/docs/react/-layout-animations

Use the `AnimatePresence` component to keep components in the DOM until their exit animations are complete, allowing elements to animate back to their origin. This is crucial for shared layout animations where an element needs to disappear gracefully.

```jsx
<AnimatePresence>
  {isOpen && <motion.div layoutId="modal" />}
</AnimatePresence>
```

--------------------------------

### AnimatePresence Modes: Sync, Wait, and PopLayout

Source: https://motion.dev/docs/react/-animate-presence

AnimatePresence offers different modes for handling entering and exiting children. 'sync' animates immediately, 'wait' sequences animations sequentially, and 'popLayout' removes elements from layout flow for immediate reflow.

```jsx
<AnimatePresence mode="wait">
  {/* Content that animates sequentially */}
</AnimatePresence>
```

```jsx
<AnimatePresence mode="popLayout">
  {items.map(item => (
    <motion.li layout exit={{ opacity: 0 }} />
  ))}
</AnimatePresence>
```

--------------------------------

### AnimatePresence Component

Source: https://motion.dev/docs/react/-animate-presence

AnimatePresence is a component that allows you to animate components when they are removed from the DOM.

```APIDOC
## AnimatePresence Component

### Description
AnimatePresence is a component that allows you to animate components when they are removed from the DOM. It provides control over exit animations and layout transitions.

### Props

#### `initial` (boolean)
- **Description**: If set to `false`, `AnimatePresence` will disable any initial animations on children that are present when the component is first rendered.
- **Example**:
```jsx
<AnimatePresence initial={false}>
  <Slide key={activeItem.id} />
</AnimatePresence>
```

#### `custom` (any)
- **Description**: Allows passing dynamic data to exit animations. This data can be accessed by children via `usePresenceData` and used to change the `exit` animation based on dynamic variants.
- **Example**:
```jsx
const variants = {
  hidden: (direction) => ({
    opacity: 0,
    x: direction === 1 ? -300 : 300
  }),
  visible: { opacity: 1, x: 0 }
}

export const Slideshow = ({ image, direction }) => (
  <AnimatePresence custom={direction}>
    <motion.img
      key={image.src}
      src={image.src}
      variants={variants}
      initial="hidden"
      animate="visible"
      exit="hidden"
    />
  </AnimatePresence>
)
```

#### `mode` (string)
- **Description**: Decides how `AnimatePresence` handles entering and exiting children. Can be one of: `"sync"`, `"wait"`, or `"popLayout"`.
  - **`"sync"` (Default)**: Elements animate in and out as soon as they're added/removed. No opinion on sequencing animations or layout.
  - **`"wait"`**: The entering element will wait until the exiting child has animated out, before it animates in. Supports only one child at a time. Great for sequential animations.
  - **`"popLayout"`**: Exiting elements will be "popped" out of the page layout, allowing surrounding elements to immediately reflow. Pairs well with the `layout` prop.
- **Example for `popLayout`**:
```jsx
<AnimatePresence mode="popLayout">
  {items.map(item => (
    <motion.li layout exit={{ opacity: 0 }} />
  ))}
</AnimatePresence>
```
- **Note for `popLayout`**: If using `popLayout` mode with custom components as immediate children, they **must** be wrapped in `React.forwardRef`.

#### `onExitComplete` (function)
- **Description**: Fires when all exiting nodes have completed animating out.

#### `propagate` (boolean)
- **Description**: If set to `true`, exit animations on children will also trigger when this `AnimatePresence` exits from a parent `AnimatePresence`. Defaults to `false`.
- **Example**:
```jsx
<AnimatePresence>
  {show ? (
    <motion.section exit={{ opacity: 0 }}>
      <AnimatePresence propagate>
        {/* This exit prop will now fire when show is false */}
        <motion.div exit={{ x: -100 }} />
      </AnimatePresence>
    </motion.section>
  ) : null}
</AnimatePresence>
```

#### `root` (Element | ShadowRoot)
- **Description**: Root element for injecting `popLayout` styles. Defaults to `document.head` but can be set to another `ShadowRoot` for use within shadow DOM.

### Troubleshooting

#### Exit animations aren't working
- Ensure all **immediate** children get a unique `key` prop that **remains the same for that component every render**.
- **Bad Key Example**:
```jsx
<AnimatePresence>
  {items.map((item, index) => (
    <Component key={index} />
  ))}
</AnimatePresence>
```
- **Preferred Key Example**:
```jsx
<AnimatePresence>
  {items.map((item) => (
    <Component key={item.id} />
  ))}
</AnimatePresence>
```
- Make sure `AnimatePresence` is **outside** of the code that unmounts the element. If `AnimatePresence` itself unmounts, it can't control exit animations.
- **Incorrect Placement Example**:
```jsx
isVisible && (
  <AnimatePresence>
    <Component />
  </AnimatePresence>
)
```
- **Correct Placement Example**:
```jsx
<AnimatePresence>
  {isVisible && <Component />}
</AnimatePresence>
```

#### Layout animations not working with `mode="sync"`
- When mixing exit and layout animations, it might be necessary to wrap the group in `LayoutGroup` to ensure that components outside of `AnimatePresence` know when to perform a layout animation.
- **Example**:
```jsx
<LayoutGroup>
  <motion.ul layout>
    <AnimatePresence>
      {items.map(item => (
        <motion.li layout key={item.id} />
      ))}
    </AnimatePresence>
  </motion.ul>
</LayoutGroup>
```
```

--------------------------------

### Implement Exit Animations with AnimatePresence

Source: https://motion.dev/docs/react/-animation

Shows how to animate elements as they are removed from the DOM using `AnimatePresence` and the `exit` prop. This component keeps elements in the DOM temporarily to allow exit animations to complete.

```jsx
<AnimatePresence>
  {isVisible && (
    <motion.div
      key="modal"
      initial={{ opacity: 0 }}
      animate={{ opacity: 1 }}
      exit={{ opacity: 0 }}
    />
  )}
</AnimatePresence>
```

--------------------------------

### AnimatePresence for Slideshows with Key Changes

Source: https://motion.dev/docs/react/-animate-presence

A practical example of using AnimatePresence with changing keys to create a slideshow effect. Each image has a unique key, allowing AnimatePresence to animate the transition between images smoothly using `initial`, `animate`, and `exit` props.

```javascript

  <AnimatePresence>
    <motion.img
      key={image.src}
      src={image.src}
      initial={{ x: 300, opacity: 0 }}
      animate={{ x: 0, opacity: 1 }}
      exit={{ x: -300, opacity: 0 }}
    />
  </AnimatePresence>
)
```

- Subagents follow TDD naturally

- Subagent can ask questions (before AND during work)

**vs. Executing Plans:**
- Same session (no handoff)

- No file reading overhead (controller provides full text)
- Controller curates exactly what context is needed
- Subagent gets complete information upfront
- Questions surfaced before work begins (not after)

**Quality gates:**
- Self-review catches issues before handoff
- Two-stage review: spec compliance, then code quality
- Review loops ensure fixes actually work
- Spec compliance prevents over/under-building
- Code quality ensures implementation is well-built

**Cost:**
- More subagent invocations (implementer + 2 reviewers per task)
- Controller does more prep work (extracting all tasks upfront)
- Review loops add iterations
- But catches issues early (cheaper than debugging later)

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Start implementation on main/master branch without explicit user consent
- Skip reviews (spec compliance OR code quality)
- Proceed with unfixed issues
- Dispatch multiple implementation subagents in parallel (conflicts)
- Make subagent read plan file (provide full text instead)
- Skip scene-setting context (subagent needs to understand where task fits)
- Ignore subagent questions (answer before letting them proceed)
- Accept "close enough" on spec compliance (spec reviewer found issues = not done)
- Skip review loops (reviewer found issues = implementer fixes = review again)
- Let implementer self-review replace actual review (both are needed)
- **Start code quality review before spec compliance is ✅** (wrong order)
- Move to next task while either review has open issues

**If subagent asks questions:**
- Answer clearly and completely
- Provide additional context if needed
- Don't rush them into implementation

**If reviewer finds issues:**
- Implementer (same subagent) fixes them
- Reviewer reviews again
- Repeat until approved
- Don't skip the re-review

**If subagent fails task:**
